Build this operation in AiService. Operations beyond the first release: generateConfiguration. Additive to AiService; its first-release owner (Pranay Shinde) reviews. Helper task: Pranay Shinde owns the service and reviews.

### `generateConfiguration` - `POST /generate/configuration`

Draft a configuration from a description. 8.8.10 to 8.8.14. **An admin describes what they want and the assistant walks the configuration** — products, pricing, promotions, seating and the calendar. Five requirements, not twenty: 8.1's "AI Configuration Assistant" heading sits over two unrelated blocks (CF-74).
**It needs no training corpus and it is not context-free**, and those are different claims. The phasing paper calls this data-independent because it forecasts nothing and learns from no history — correct. But *"create VIP seating in the first three rows with a 30% premium"* cannot be answered without the seat map, the price categories and the venue's own vocabulary.
**So it reads the venue's current configuration and nothing behavioural.** Twenty-two tables: the catalogue, price lists, promotions, the seat map, performances and region settings. No orders, no scans, no guests.
**The bootstrapping case is the one to design for.** A brand-new tenant has no seat map, no price list and no products, and *"first three rows"* means nothing. On an empty venue the assistant creates rather than amends, and the two are different prompts with different risk — **amending touches things already sold.**
**Proposes; never applies.** Writes `ai.proposed_action` and stops. 8.1.4 requires approval before execution for anything affecting pricing or financial operations, and this is that gate — the same one `x-ticvai-permission-escalated` enforces for a human.
Seating includes generating a map from an uploaded layout, which is `generateVenueLayout` and `importSeatGeometry` (CF-123). **The assistant does not parse the drawing** — it names the sections, categories and premiums once the geometry is in.

- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 A draft, plus what it needed to guess -> GeneratedConfiguration
- **Reads:** ai.chunk_ref, ai.policy, ai.provider, cache:idempotency, catalogue.variant_dimension, catalogue.entitlement_template, catalogue.channel_capacity, catalogue.event, catalogue.performance, catalogue.price, catalogue.price_list, catalogue.product, marketing.loyalty_programme, platform.region_settings, platform.scope, promotions.promotion, qdrant:knowledge, seating.seat, seating.seat_category, seating.seat_map, seating.seating_rules, seating.section; **writes:** ai.activity, ai.proposed_action, cache:idempotency, qdrant:knowledge

18457:
Build these 4 operations in OrderService. Operations beyond the first release: authoriseStoredValue, captureStoredValue, createGroupBooking, relinquishStoredValue. Additive to OrderService; its first-release owner (Pranay Shinde) reviews.

### `authoriseStoredValue` - `POST /stored-value/authorisations`

Hold a balance on any stored-value instrument. CF-126. **`authoriseWalletSpend` did this for the retail wallet and for nothing else**, so a guest with 200 game credits starting a play the machine then failed had no held balance — the credits were either taken or not, with no third state.
Works against a wallet, a gift card, a game card, a voucher, a loyalty position or a prepaid entitlement. **The instruments stay distinct; the spend mechanism is shared.**
Refuses where the balance is insufficient **after existing holds**, which is what stops the same credits being committed twice.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/orders.yaml` (operationId `authoriseStoredValue`)
- **Permission:** ORDER_CREATE, checked at venue level; audience staff, guest, device
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 201 Held -> StoredValueAuthorisation; 409 Insufficient balance after existing holds. **The reason says which**, because *"insufficient funds"* on a card the guest just topped up is a support call.

- **Reads:** orders.stored_value_authorisation, promotions.voucher, wallet.gift_card, wallet.wallet; **writes:** cache:idempotency, orders.stored_value_authorisation
- **Service:** OrderService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-097 Check Out & Check In (P08)

### `captureStoredValue` - `POST /stored-value/authorisations/{authorisationId}/capture`

Take some or all of a held balance. Partial capture is the normal case, not the exception — **a tab authorised at 200 and settled at 140**, or an arcade play that cost less than the hold.
The remainder stays held until released or expired.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/orders.yaml` (operationId `captureStoredValue`)
- **Permission:** ORDER_CREATE, checked at venue level; audience staff, device
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 Captured -> StoredValueAuthorisation
- **Reads:** orders.stored_value_authorisation; **writes:** cache:idempotency, orders.stored_value_authorisation, wallet.wallet_transaction
- **Service:** OrderService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-097 Check Out & Check In (P08)

### `createGroupBooking` - `POST /group-bookings`

Turn an order into a group booking. BL-028. **`getGroupBooking` read a table nothing wrote**, so `BO-026 Group Bookings` still ran on generic order operations: no leader, no expected size, no names to collect.
**A group booking wraps an order; it does not replace one.** The order holds the tickets and the money; this holds the leader, the size and the name-capture duty. One order carries at most one group booking.
Starts `provisional`, or `namesPending` when `attendeeCaptureRequired` is set.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/orders.yaml` (operationId `createGroupBooking`)
- **Permission:** ORDER_CREATE, checked at venue level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** CreateGroupBookingRequest
- **Responses:** 201 Created -> GroupBooking; 400 BadRequest; 403 Forbidden; 409 The order already has a group booking, or is voided.
- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, orders.group_booking, orders.sales_order, pii.subject; **writes:** cache:idempotency, orders.group_booking
- **Service:** OrderService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-026 Group Bookings (P08)

### `relinquishStoredValue` - `POST /stored-value/authorisations/{authorisationId}/release`

Give a hold back. The play failed, the guest left, the tab closed short. **Released holds return immediately** — and expiry releases automatically, because a hold nobody releases is a guest whose balance is short with no explanation.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/orders.yaml` (operationId `relinquishStoredValue`)
- **Permission:** ORDER_CREATE, checked at venue level; audience staff, device
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Responses:** 200 Released -> StoredValueAuthorisation
- **Reads:** orders.stored_value_authorisation; **writes:** nothing
- **Service:** OrderService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-097 Check Out & Check In (P08)

### `createApprovalDelegation` - `POST /delegations`

Delegate approval authority. 11.1.9. **Always time-bounded.** An open-ended delegation is an approver who quietly stopped approving months ago and a delegate who does not know they still hold it.
The delegate cannot exceed the delegator's own authority, and **cannot approve a request the delegator raised** — segregation of duties survives delegation, or delegation becomes the way around it.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/approvals.yaml` (operationId `createApprovalDelegation`)
- **Permission:** APPROVAL_DECIDE, checked at venue level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** ApprovalDelegation
- **Responses:** 201 Delegated -> ApprovalDelegation; 403 The delegate does not hold the permission being delegated
- **Reads:** approvals.delegation, cache:idempotency, identity.delegated_access, identity.principal; **writes:** approvals.delegation, cache:idempotency
- **Service:** TenancyService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-087 Approval Delegations (P08)

### `setApprovalMatrix` - `PUT /approval-matrices`

Configure what requires approval. 11.1.2. Rules are ordered and **the first match wins**, so adding a rule cannot silently change an unrelated one. A matrix with overlapping unordered rules is a matrix nobody can reason about, and the ordering is the thing that makes it reviewable.
Changing a matrix creates a version (11.1.80). Requests in flight keep the version they were raised under — **a request must be decided by the rules it was raised under**, or an approver is answering a question that changed while they read it.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/approvals.yaml` (operationId `setApprovalMatrix`)
- **Permission:** APPROVAL_CONFIGURE, checked at venue level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** ApprovalMatrix
- **Responses:** 200 Set, as a new version -> ApprovalMatrix; 409 The matrix would loosen a rule set at a higher scope, or a rule is unreachable behind an earlier one.

- **Reads:** approvals.matrix, approvals.rule, cache:idempotency; **writes:** approvals.matrix, approvals.rule, cache:idempotency
- **Service:** TenancyService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins

### `deleteGuestAccount` - `DELETE /auth/guest/account`

Self-service account deletion. Raises an erasure request rather than deleting immediately. PII is removed from the erasable store; ledger entries keep their opaque subject reference and stay intact.
Where the guest is linked across cells, the request fans out (ADR-0010).

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/identity.yaml` (operationId `deleteGuestAccount`)
- **Permission:** none named, checked at tenant level; audience guest
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Responses:** 202 Erasure request raised -> object; 409 Open orders or an unexpired entitlement exist. Deleting an account with a valid ticket in it strands the guest at a gate.

- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, pii.subject; **writes:** cache:idempotency, pii.subject, platform.dsar_request
- **Service:** IdentityService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** GST-066 Privacy & My Data (P02), WEB-024 Devices, Wishlist & Consent (P01)

### `runReport` - `POST /reports/{reportId}/run`

Run a report. Executes against the **reporting replica**, never the primary.
Small results return inline. Anything beyond the inline threshold returns `202` with an execution to poll — a synchronous response containing a year of scan events is a timeout waiting to happen.
Scope is applied from the caller's resolved permissions. Parameters narrow; they never widen.

- **Contract:** `contracts/satellite/reporting.yaml` (operationId `runReport`)
- **Permission:** REPORT_VIEW_VENUE, checked at venue level; audience staff, partner
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** RunReportRequest
- **Responses:** 200 Completed inline -> ReportResult; 202 Queued. Poll the execution -> ReportExecution; 400 Required parameter missing, or the date range exceeds the limit; 403 Forbidden

### `ingestFxRates` - `POST /fx-rates/ingest`

Pull rates from the configured provider. **Scheduled ingestion, which had no home.** `setFxRate` is a `PUT` carrying `setByPrincipalId` — a person setting a rate — so a daily provider pull had to be modelled as a person doing it, and the ledger could not tell an automated rate from a typed one.

**Ingests per purpose, not per currency pair.** `FxRatePurpose` has four values and they are four different rates on the same day: `tender` is what a guest pays at, `reporting` is a period-end consolidation rate, `revaluation` restates open obligations, `interEntity` is a transfer price that is often deliberately not the market rate. **A feed that overwrites one number breaks the other three.**

**Never overwrites.** A new rate is a new row with its own `effectiveFrom` — that is what lets a month-end be re-run and give the same answer, and why `runFxRevaluation` can be dry-run.

**Refused if the provider is unreachable rather than falling back to the last rate.** A stale rate silently reused is worse than a missing one: the first is wrong and looks right.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/finance.yaml` (operationId `ingestFxRates`)
- **Permission:** LEDGER_APPROVE, checked at region level; audience staff, service
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 What was fetched -> object
- **Reads:** ledger.fx_rate, platform.region_settings; **writes:** cache:idempotency, ledger.fx_rate
- **Service:** LedgerService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: append
- **Used by:** BO-077 FX Rates & Variances (P08)

### `listFxRates` - `GET /fx-rates`

The rates in force. **Policy, settled 14 August: every transaction is stored in the base currency of the region it was transacted in.**
A guest paying USD 100 in a UAE venue has the dirham equivalent stored at the configured rate. The foreign amount is retained for the cashier's declaration and for the foreign-tender report — it is never what the ledger holds.
The consequence is that most of the questions FX usually raises do not arise. There is no rate to lock at redemption, none at expiry, and none at refund, because the stored amount was never in a foreign currency. Allam: *"the value of the currency doesn't matter whether it goes high or down. They are purchasing a product equivalent to that currency… at the end they are paying that base currency value, and they get a refund for the base currency value."*

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/finance.yaml` (operationId `listFxRates`)
- **Permission:** LEDGER_VIEW, checked at region level; audience staff, guest
- **Parameters:** `asAt` (query, string (date-time)), `purpose` (query, FxRatePurpose), `PageSize` (shared), `PageCursor` (shared)
- **Responses:** 200 Rates -> list of FxRate
- **Reads:** ledger.fx_rate; **writes:** nothing
- **Service:** LedgerService; reads routed to replica; offline-capable: yes; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-077 FX Rates & Variances (P08), GST-044 Multi-Currency & Pricing (P02), WEB-035 Multi-Currency & Pricing (P01)

### `setFxRate` - `PUT /fx-rates`

Set a rate. Rates are **configured, not fetched live**. A published market rate moving mid-shift would mean two guests paying different dirham amounts for the same product minutes apart, and a cashier unable to explain either.
A rate change is a new row with its own effective window; the old one is never edited. A transaction posted last Tuesday must still reconcile at last Tuesday's rate.
**Tender rates carry a spread.** The rate a venue accepts dollars at is not the interbank rate, and pretending otherwise makes every foreign-tender sale look like a small loss.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/finance.yaml` (operationId `setFxRate`)
- **Permission:** LEDGER_APPROVE, checked at region level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** FxRate
- **Responses:** 201 Set -> FxRate; 409 Effective window overlaps an existing rate for the same pair and purpose
- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, ledger.fx_rate; **writes:** cache:idempotency, ledger.fx_rate
- **Service:** LedgerService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-077 FX Rates & Variances (P08)

### `importVenueGeometry` - `POST /venue-maps/{mapId}/import`

Read a drawing into shapes. 21.2.1 to 21.2.4 and 1.4.24. **Deterministic, and it fails loudly.**
Accepts what a venue's drawing office actually holds: PDF, SVG, DWG, DXF and raster. **Converting CAD to PDF loses the layer names this depends on**, which is why native formats are accepted rather than requested as exports.
Carries every lesson CF-122 taught on the seat importer, because it is the same problem: **layer roles are lists** — one real file had two distinct layers both named `Layer 1`; **section codes are digit-normalised** — `A١` and `A1` are one place to a person and two to a comparison; **layer names are decoded before matching** — PDF strings arrive UTF-16BE and read as mojibake taken as bytes.
**A file that yields no shapes reports `nothingFound`, not success.**

- **Contract:** `contracts/satellite/venue-map.yaml` (operationId `importVenueGeometry`)
- **Permission:** VENUE_MAP_MANAGE, checked at venue level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 202 Extracted to a draft -> VenueMapImportJob
- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, venuemap.import_job, venuemap.map; **writes:** cache:idempotency, venuemap.import_job, venuemap.path, venuemap.point
- **Service:** VenueOpsService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-093 Map Import & Labelling (P08)

Find something by name. **The guest app browses by category and cannot search.** On a venue with two hundred products that is the difference between finding a thing and giving up.
Distinct from `semanticSearch`, which is AI and retrieves from documents. This is a keyword search over the sellable catalogue, and it works with no AI configured — a venue without an assistant still needs a search box.

### `transitionProductLifecycle` - `POST /products/{productId}/lifecycle`

Move a product through its lifecycle. Draft → review → approved → live → withdrawn → archived.
**Approval is separate from publication.** An approved product is not sellable until a bundle carries it, which is why the two are different acts with different permissions — a product manager approves, an operator publishes.
Withdrawal stops new sales and leaves existing entitlements intact. Archiving is refused while entitlements remain unexpired.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/catalogue.yaml` (operationId `transitionProductLifecycle`)
- **Permission:** PRODUCT_CONFIGURE, checked at venue level; audience staff, partner
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 Transitioned -> Product; 403 Approval attempted by the principal who submitted it. Segregation applies here as it does to journals.
; 409 Transition not valid from the current state, or archiving attempted while unexpired entitlements exist.

### `joinWaitlist` - `POST /waitlist-entries`

Ask to be told if capacity frees up. 1.1.25, 4.9.17. **Offered only where the session is genuinely sold out** — a waitlist on something available is a worse experience than selling it.
**Joining reserves nothing.** The guest is told when capacity appears and buys like anyone else, because holding capacity for a waitlist is the same as not releasing it.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/catalogue.yaml` (operationId `joinWaitlist`)
- **Permission:** none named, checked at venue level; audience guest
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** WaitlistEntry
- **Responses:** 201 Joined -> WaitlistEntry; 409 The session is not sold out. **Refused rather than accepted**, because a waitlist entry on available capacity will never be notified and the guest will wait forever.

- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, catalogue.channel_capacity, catalogue.performance, catalogue.waitlist_entry; **writes:** cache:idempotency, catalogue.waitlist_entry
- **Service:** CatalogueService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** GST-070 Reserve a Table or Cabana (P02), WEB-040 Virtual Queue (P01)

### `listGuestMemberships` - `GET /guest/memberships`

A guest's memberships, benefits and history. 19.2.26 to 19.2.28. **`membership` is a `ProductKind`, so purchase and renewal already ride the order path — and nothing returned a guest their own memberships.**
Three requirements and one operation, because they are one screen: what I hold, what it entitles me to, and what I held before.
**Tier benefits come from the product, not from a separate benefits table** (5.4.31). A benefit nobody can trace to the thing that grants it is a benefit nobody can honour at a gate.
Lapsed terms are included — **a guest who let a pass expire is the guest most worth showing a renewal to**, and hiding the history hides the reason.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/catalogue.yaml` (operationId `listGuestMemberships`)
- **Permission:** PRODUCT_VIEW, checked at venue level; audience staff, guest
- **Parameters:** `includeLapsed` (query, boolean), `PageSize` (shared), `PageCursor` (shared)
- **Responses:** 200 Memberships, current first -> list of GuestMembership
- **Reads:** catalogue.entitlement_template, catalogue.product, orders.sales_order; **writes:** nothing
- **Service:** CatalogueService; reads routed to replica; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** GST-015 Memberships (P02), WEB-022 Membership Plans (P01), WEB-023 Membership Management (P01)

Add something. 2.9.4. **Acquiring the lease is the whole reason this is a server operation.** A capacity-bound product added to a cart reserves capacity for a configured window, and a cart held in a browser cannot reserve anything.

- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, catalogue.channel_capacity, catalogue.performance, catalogue.variant, orders.cart, orders.cart_line; **writes:** cache:idempotency, catalogue.inventory_hold, orders.cart, orders.cart_line

### `checkoutCart` - `POST /carts/{cartId}/checkout`

Turn the cart into an order. **Transfers the leases to the order rather than releasing and re-acquiring them.** Releasing first would let another guest take the capacity between the two calls, which is the failure that makes a checkout feel unreliable at exactly the wrong moment.
The cart is retained, not deleted — a checkout that fails at payment must be resumable, and a guest whose card was declined should still have their seats.
**One cart, one order, one receipt** across ticketing, F&B and retail (14 August).
**No order against an unproven contact on the guest web or app** (decided 17 September 2026; the rule is on `identity` `verifyGuestEmail`). A signed-in session must be verified; where the site's `guestCheckout` feature is on, a guest without an account must have proved the email or mobile the tickets go to with a one-time code. **Kiosk walk-up orders are exempt** — the tickets are printed for the person standing there.
**This operation is the gate, and the cart is not** ([ADR-0045](../../docs/adr/0045-every-order-carries-a-proven-contact.md), 18 September 2026, matrix 2.6.1 §2.4). Anyone may fill a cart. The fork between signing in and supplying guest details belongs to the checkout page — `WEB-011`, `GST-041` — and this call refuses until one of them has completed, keeping the cart so the guest resumes rather than restarts.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/orders.yaml` (operationId `checkoutCart`)
- **Permission:** none named, checked at venue level; audience guest, partner
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 201 An order, pending payment -> Order; 403 The contact the tickets would go to is not proven — an unverified session, or a guest checkout with no confirmed one-time code. **The client sends the guest to sign-in or to the code step and keeps the cart**; nothing is released.
; 409 A lease expired between the last read and checkout. **Names which line**, so the guest loses one thing rather than the cart.

- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, catalogue.inventory_hold, orders.cart, orders.cart_line, orders.order_line, orders.payment, orders.sales_order; **writes:** cache:idempotency, orders.cart, orders.order_line, orders.sales_order

Add something to a ticket the guest already holds. A guest arrives, buys admission, and an hour later wants a locker. They scan the QR they are already carrying and the locker attaches to it. **No second QR.**

### `recordOrderHandover` - `POST /guest-orders/{orderId}/delivery`

Record that an order reached the guest. The closing state, and it differs by fulfilment: a server marks `served`, a counter marks `collected`, a runner marks `delivered`. 4.6.35 distinguishes all three, and so does this — "the guest has it" is not one event when the dispute is about which.
Offline-capable. A runner crossing a venue loses signal, and an order that cannot be closed until they return is an order that reads as undelivered for ten minutes.

### `enrolFacePass` - `POST /face-pass/enrolments`

Register a facial profile against an entitlement. 3.2.43. **Registrable only through the app, a ticket counter or the annual pass counter** — never at a gate, and never at a kiosk. The requirement names the three surfaces and the omission is the point: enrolment is a considered act with consent attached, not something done in a queue.
**One facial profile may not be associated with more than one annual pass.** The refusal is explicit rather than a unique constraint, because the reason matters to the person at the counter — a duplicate means either a mistake or a pass being shared.
**Consent is captured in the same transaction and is not implied by enrolment.** Under PDPL a biometric is a special category, and a consent record written afterwards is a consent record for something that already happened.
**A minor's consent is given by a guardian**, and the guardian is recorded. The child-protection journey (3.2.12) sits above this.
No image is stored — a template is. **The template cannot reconstruct the face**, and that is the property that makes retention defensible at all (CF-35, CF-64).

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/access.yaml` (operationId `enrolFacePass`)
- **Permission:** GUEST_MANAGE, checked at venue level; audience staff, guest
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 201 Enrolled -> FacePassEnrolment; 409 **This face is already on another annual pass.** Returned with the reason and without naming the other pass — a counter agent needs to know it is a duplicate, not whose.
; 422 Capture quality too low to enrol. Retake rather than store something that will not match.
- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, marketing.consent_record, pii.subject, pii.subject_biometric; **writes:** cache:idempotency, marketing.consent_record, pii.subject_biometric
- **Service:** AccessService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** GST-069 Face Pass (P02)

### `changeOwnCredential` - `POST /auth/credential`

Change the caller's own password or PIN. **`createPrincipal` defaults `mustChangeCredential` to true and nothing could change a credential**, so every new member of staff was issued an initial secret they could never replace: the first sign-in could not complete. `identity.principal_credential` was read by `login` and written by nothing after creation.
**The current credential is required even inside a session.** A till left signed in is a session somebody else can use, and changing its PIN without knowing the old one is how that session becomes theirs permanently.
Held to `setPasswordPolicy` (length, breach check); a PIN is held to the length rule only, because it is valid only on a registered workstation (see `LoginRequest.method`). **Every other session of the principal is ended** on success, since a credential changed because it leaked is not fixed while the leaked one is still signed in.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/identity.yaml` (operationId `changeOwnCredential`)
- **Permission:** none named, checked at tenant level; audience staff, partner
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** ChangeCredentialRequest
- **Responses:** 204 Changed. Other sessions of this principal are ended.; 400 BadRequest; 401 Unauthorized; 422 The new credential fails the password policy, or is the same as the current one.
- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, identity.principal, identity.principal_credential, identity.password_policy; **writes:** cache:idempotency, identity.principal_credential, identity.session

### `verifyGuestEmail` - `POST /auth/guest/verify-email`

Send a verification link, or consume one. **Raised in review by Deep.** `registerGuest` creates an account and nothing verifies the address on it — and **a guest account with an unverified email can receive somebody else's tickets**, because a transfer is offered to an address.
Two modes on one operation: **`send` issues a single-use token; `confirm` consumes it.** One operation because they are one act with two halves, and splitting them invites a `confirm` that works without a `send`.
**An unverified account does not buy — decided 17 September 2026**, replacing *unverified accounts still buy*, which this description said while `registerGuest` and `GuestSession.isVerified` said the opposite. Tickets go to an address, and an unproven address is how somebody receives a stranger's tickets.
**On the guest web and the guest app, the site's `guestCheckout` feature decides the route** (requirement matrix 2.6.28 and 2.6.67 — guest checkout, configurable per site). It is **off by default**.
**The gate is the checkout page, not the cart** ([ADR-0045](../../docs/adr/0045-every-order-carries-a-proven-contact.md), 18 September 2026, matrix 2.6.1 §2.4: *"On the check out page, users can log in or manually fill in the following details"*). The cart is open to anyone; `checkoutCart` refuses until one of the two routes has completed.
- **Off:** the guest signs in, verified, at checkout. `WEB-011` and `GST-041` carry the fork.
- **On:** the guest may check out without an account, and proves the email or mobile the tickets go to with a one-time code at checkout (`requestGuestOtp`, purpose `verify`) — the *dual OTP validation* of the reference checkout the client walked through.
**Both routes produce a guest profile**, because the tickets have to go somewhere and the order has to belong to something. **A one-time checkout profile carries no credential** — recalling previous transactions needs access set up separately (matrix 2.6.29), which is what `linkGuestCheckout` does from the other direction.
**A returning verified contact attaches to the profile already held** (matrix 22.2.8) — the new order, its tickets and its history, automatically, with no duplicate record. **It does not open that profile.** The guest sees the order just placed and nothing earlier until they authenticate as its owner: a code proves someone controls the mailbox today, which is enough to route a ticket there and not enough to hand over a history. **Any match that is not a verified contact** — passport, national id, an unproved phone, a similar name — **is a suggestion for the staff review of matrix 7.3.7**, with its audit log and rollback. A merge takes the narrower of two consents (CF-160).
**The kiosk is exempt.** A walk-up pays at the kiosk and takes printed tickets, so there is no address to prove (matrix 2.1.10). An unverified account also cannot *receive a transfer* or *reset a password*, for the same reason.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/identity.yaml` (operationId `verifyGuestEmail`)
- **Permission:** GUEST_VIEW, checked at tenant level; audience guest, anonymous
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 Sent, or verified -> object; 410 **The token expired or was already used.** Distinct from an invalid one — a guest who clicked an old link should be offered a new one rather than told they are wrong.

- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, identity.otp_challenge, pii.subject; **writes:** cache:idempotency, identity.otp_challenge, marketing.message_dispatch, pii.subject
- **Service:** IdentityService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** GST-073 Security & Sign-in (P02), WEB-020 Profile & Preferences (P01)

### `requestSuggestion` - `POST /ai/suggestions`

Ask for an answer, however it is currently produced. **One operation for thirteen questions, and the reason is the swap.** The client F&B boards drew six of these as their own endpoints — `suggestPrice`, `suggestRequisition`, `suggestReplenishment`, `simulateScenario`, `simulateSlaPolicy`, `publishDemandPlan`. **Six endpoints means six places to change when a model changes**, and the model will change more often than the venue's question does.
**Ships answering from heuristics.** A price suggestion is a margin rule; a replenishment is par level minus on-hand plus lead time. **Every one of those is a stated rule that works on day one and is beaten by a model on day four hundred** — and the swap is a provider change, not a contract change.
**The response always names its basis.** A manager must be able to see that today's answer is arithmetic and next quarter's is a trained model, on the same screen, without being told.
**Never acts.** A suggestion that can order stock is a suggestion that will order stock wrongly at three in the morning — this proposes, and `decideProposedAction` decides.

- **Contract:** `contracts/satellite/ai.yaml` (operationId `requestSuggestion`)
- **Permission:** AI_USE, checked at venue level; audience staff, guest
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 The suggestion, with its basis and its reasoning -> Suggestion; 422 **Not enough data to answer.** A venue three weeks old has no seasonality, and **refusing is better than a confident number built on nothing** — the response names what is missing and when there will be enough.

- **Reads:** ai.policy, ai.provider, ai.suggestion, cache:idempotency; **writes:** ai.activity, ai.suggestion, cache:idempotency
- **Service:** AiService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins

Retrieval runs **as the calling principal**. The assistant can see exactly what that person could have read directly and nothing more — no service account, no elevated query. This is the difference between an assistant and a privilege escalation with a friendly interface.
Every response carries a trace id, the model and provider that produced it, token counts and its sources. Not for the user's benefit: for cost attribution and for the grounding audit that 8.3.70 requires.
**Where the answer proposes an action, it is a draft.** The response carries a `proposedAction` the caller may apply through the owning contract, and applying it is a separate, permissioned, audited step (8.3.61–8.3.64).

- **Contract:** `contracts/satellite/ai.yaml` (operationId `sendAiMessage`)
- **Permission:** AI_USE, checked at venue level; audience staff, guest
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 Answered -> AiMessage; 429 Usage limit reached for this tenant or principal (8.3.76). The limit is a cost control, and the message says which limit rather than failing opaquely.
; 503 Every configured provider failed. **Reported rather than retried indefinitely** — an assistant that hangs is worse than one that says it cannot answer.

- **Reads:** ai.chunk_ref, ai.conversation, ai.knowledge_document, ai.message, ai.policy, ai.proposed_action, ai.provider, cache:answer, cache:idempotency, qdrant:knowledge; **writes:** ai.activity, ai.message, ai.proposed_action, cache:answer, cache:idempotency, qdrant:knowledge
- **Service:** AiService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: append

### `askReportingQuestion` - `POST /reports/ask`

Natural-language reporting query. **This is an AI capability and is governed as one.** It resolves its provider through `ai.provider`, respects `ai.policy` including the masking list, and writes an `ai.interaction` with its prompt, response, model, tokens and cost — the same audit trail as the assistant (8.3.55–8.3.57).
Distinct from `sendAiMessage`, which retrieves from documents. **This generates a query against the analytical replica and returns it**, so a finance user can check the number rather than trust it.

### `setParkingFacility` - `PUT /parking-facilities`

Configure a car park and its integration. **The mode is the decision, and the three are not variations of one thing.**
`none` — TICVAI issues its own QR and security verifies it by eye. No integration, and the guest experience depends on a person.
`plateWhitelist` — the guest gives a plate at checkout and the platform pushes it to the parking system's whitelist. **The barrier opens without anything being presented**, which is the best experience and the only mode that needs a plate captured at sale.
`qrHandoff` — TICVAI sends a code the barrier validates. No plate needed, and it fails the way any code fails: a dead phone at a barrier with a queue behind it.
A fourth case is out of scope: pay-per-hour parking unrelated to a ticket runs on the parking system's own POS (14 August).

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/access.yaml` (operationId `setParkingFacility`)
- **Permission:** PARKING_CONFIGURE, checked at venue level; audience staff

- **Request body:** ParkingFacility

- **Reads:** access.parking_facility, cache:idempotency; **writes:** access.parking_facility, cache:idempotency

### `createGoodsReceipt` - `POST /goods-receipts`

Receive goods against a purchase order. Partial receipts are normal and expected. Over-receipt beyond the configured tolerance is refused — a delivery larger than the order is a supplier error, not a windfall.
Receipt increments stock and creates the accrual the invoice will later match against.

- **Contract:** `contracts/satellite/inventory.yaml` (operationId `createGoodsReceipt`)
- **Permission:** PRODUCT_CONFIGURE, checked at venue level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** CreateGoodsReceiptRequest
- **Responses:** 201 Received; stock incremented -> GoodsReceipt; 409 Over-receipt beyond tolerance, or the purchase order is closed
- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, inventory.goods_receipt, inventory.goods_receipt_line; **writes:** cache:idempotency, inventory.goods_receipt, platform.outbox
- **Service:** InventoryService; offline-capable: yes; conflicts: append
- **Used by:** BO-052 Goods Receipt (P08), BO-080 Stock Transfers (P08), EMP-065 Receiving & Store Put-Away (P06)

### `createApiClient` - `POST /api-clients`

Create a client with scopes and an environment. 13.1.11 to 13.1.13, and **CF-135a: the credential model was owned by nobody.** 2.7.52, 7.1.25 and 7.1.30 each asserted their own, so a partner API key, a POS integration credential and a webstore credential were three unrelated things. **This is the one that exists.**
**A client is bound to one environment.** A sandbox client cannot reach production, which is stated on the object rather than enforced by a naming convention — **a key that works in both is a key somebody will use in the wrong one.**

- **Permission:** DEVELOPER_MANAGE, checked at tenant level; audience staff, partner
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** ApiClient
- **Responses:** 201 Created. **The secret is returned once and never again** — a system that can show you a secret later is a system that stores one.
 -> object

### `closeWorkOrder` - `POST /work-orders/{workOrderId}/close`

Administratively closed. 18.2.7. **Not the same as completing or verifying it.** Completion is the technician saying the work is done; verification is someone else agreeing; closing is the supervisor deciding the record needs no further action.
Used where a job was completed and verified, and equally where it was overtaken by events — the asset was replaced, the fault did not recur, the venue closed the area. **A work order that can only end by being completed is one that stays open forever when the answer is "never mind".**

- **Contract:** `contracts/satellite/maintenance.yaml` (operationId `closeWorkOrder`)
- **Permission:** MAINTENANCE_APPROVE, checked at venue level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 Closed -> WorkOrder
- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, maintenance.asset, maintenance.work_order; **writes:** cache:idempotency, maintenance.work_order

### `getChannelAllocations` - `GET /channel-capacities/{channelCapacityId}/channel-allocations`

Capacity allocated to each channel. How much of an envelope each selling channel may take. Revenue management sets this; a lease draws from it.
Allocation is the commercial concern, a lease is the technical one, and they compose: a lease is granted against a channel's remaining allocation rather than against raw envelope capacity. Web cannot consume the counter's allocation, and an offline terminal cannot oversell a channel it was never given.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/catalogue.yaml` (operationId `getChannelAllocations`)
- **Permission:** PRODUCT_VIEW, checked at venue level; audience staff, partner
- **Responses:** 200 Allocations -> ChannelAllocationSet; 404 NotFound
- **Reads:** catalogue.channel_allocation; **writes:** nothing
- **Service:** CatalogueService; reads routed to primary; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-013 Channel & Distribution (P08), BO-017 Capacity Management (P08); later: P06 EMP-033 Capacity view, P10 PTR-005 Inventory & Allocation View

Set the attribute axes for a product. Attributes are axes that generate sellable variants. Changing them triggers variant regeneration; the response reports how many variants result.

### `testQueueFeed` - `POST /queue-feeds/{feedId}/test`

Test a feed before trusting it. Attempts one exchange with the configured source and reports what came back — reachable, authenticated, and whether the payload parsed into a reading the platform understands.
Configuring an integration without a test is configuring it blind. The failure this catches is the common one: credentials accepted, endpoint reachable, and the payload in a shape nobody mapped — which looks like silence rather than an error.
Readings from a test are discarded. A test must not move a wait time on a live board.

- **Contract:** `contracts/satellite/queue.yaml` (operationId `testQueueFeed`)
- **Permission:** QUEUE_MANAGE, checked at venue level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Responses:** 200 Test complete. Check `succeeded` — a reachable source that returns nonsense is a failure -> FeedTestResult; 404 NotFound
- **Reads:** cache:idempotency, queue.reading; **writes:** cache:idempotency, queue.reading
- **Service:** VenueOpsService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-001 Queue Directory (P08), BO-003 Queue Integration Setup (P08)

### `bookResource` - `POST /resource-bookings`

Reserve a specific resource for a window — staff only. **Refuses on conflict, including setup and teardown.** This is the operation the whole context exists for — **two bookings on one cabana is a guest arriving to find somebody in their chair**, and it must be impossible rather than unlikely.
Where the caller does not care which one, `resourceId` may be omitted and a kind supplied: **the platform picks and tells you which.**
## Amended 19 September — no longer guest-callable
This shipped with `x-ticvai-guest-callable: true`, and the 26 August minute says otherwise:
> *"a guest always books a product or package — **never a resource directly, and never a specific room/vehicle/instructor by itself** — across all sales channels. The product's configuration determines which resources are associated and get booked behind the scenes."*
**The original reasoning was right and stopped one step short.** It argued a guest booking *a* cabana does not choose cabana seven; the minute goes further and says the guest does not address the cabana at all. They buy a product, the product declares what it needs (`setExperienceResourceRequirements`), and `allocateResources` fills it — rotating, per the same minute, so one cabana is not worn out while others sit empty.
**This closes the open question on `F25-a-guest-rents-a-cabana`**, which recorded that the venue had not said whether a guest may book a cabana themselves. They had; it was minuted on 26 August and nothing read the minutes.

### `generateConfiguration` - `POST /generate/configuration`

Draft a configuration from a description. 8.8.10 to 8.8.14. **An admin describes what they want and the assistant walks the configuration** — products, pricing, promotions, seating and the calendar. Five requirements, not twenty: 8.1's "AI Configuration Assistant" heading sits over two unrelated blocks (CF-74).
**It needs no training corpus and it is not context-free**, and those are different claims. The phasing paper calls this data-independent because it forecasts nothing and learns from no history — correct. But *"create VIP seating in the first three rows with a 30% premium"* cannot be answered without the seat map, the price categories and the venue's own vocabulary.
**So it reads the venue's current configuration and nothing behavioural.** Twenty-two tables: the catalogue, price lists, promotions, the seat map, performances and region settings. No orders, no scans, no guests.
**The bootstrapping case is the one to design for.** A brand-new tenant has no seat map, no price list and no products, and *"first three rows"* means nothing. On an empty venue the assistant creates rather than amends, and the two are different prompts with different risk — **amending touches things already sold.**
**Proposes; never applies.** Writes `ai.proposed_action` and stops. 8.1.4 requires approval before execution for anything affecting pricing or financial operations, and this is that gate — the same one `x-ticvai-permission-escalated` enforces for a human.
Seating includes generating a map from an uploaded layout, which is `generateVenueLayout` and `importSeatGeometry` (CF-123). **The assistant does not parse the drawing** — it names the sections, categories and premiums once the geometry is in.

- **Contract:** `contracts/satellite/ai.yaml` (operationId `generateConfiguration`)
- **Permission:** AI_USE, checked at venue level; audience staff
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 200 A draft, plus what it needed to guess -> GeneratedConfiguration
- **Reads:** ai.chunk_ref, ai.policy, ai.provider, cache:idempotency, catalogue.variant_dimension, catalogue.entitlement_template, catalogue.channel_capacity, catalogue.event, catalogue.performance, catalogue.price, catalogue.price_list, catalogue.product, marketing.loyalty_programme, platform.region_settings, platform.scope, promotions.promotion, qdrant:knowledge, seating.seat, seating.seat_category, seating.seat_map, seating.seating_rules, seating.section; **writes:** ai.activity, ai.proposed_action, cache:idempotency, qdrant:knowledge
- **Service:** AiService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-117 Product Import, Governance & AI Configuration Assistant (P08); later: P08 BO-597 AI Configuration Workspace, P08 BO-598 AI Draft Review & Approval

What else this guest might want. BL-068. **Rule-based recommendation exists; profile-and-cart-driven does not**, and the difference is whether a guest who has already bought a family ticket is offered another one.

### `authoriseStoredValue` - `POST /stored-value/authorisations`

Hold a balance on any stored-value instrument. CF-126. **`authoriseWalletSpend` did this for the retail wallet and for nothing else**, so a guest with 200 game credits starting a play the machine then failed had no held balance — the credits were either taken or not, with no third state.
Works against a wallet, a gift card, a game card, a voucher, a loyalty position or a prepaid entitlement. **The instruments stay distinct; the spend mechanism is shared.**
Refuses where the balance is insufficient **after existing holds**, which is what stops the same credits being committed twice.

- **Contract:** `contracts/spine/orders.yaml` (operationId `authoriseStoredValue`)
- **Permission:** ORDER_CREATE, checked at venue level; audience staff, guest, device
- **Parameters:** `IdempotencyKey` (shared)
- **Request body:** object
- **Responses:** 201 Held -> StoredValueAuthorisation; 409 Insufficient balance after existing holds. **The reason says which**, because *"insufficient funds"* on a card the guest just topped up is a support call.

- **Reads:** orders.stored_value_authorisation, promotions.voucher, wallet.gift_card, wallet.wallet; **writes:** cache:idempotency, orders.stored_value_authorisation
- **Service:** OrderService; offline-capable: no; conflicts: serverWins
- **Used by:** BO-097 Check Out & Check In (P08)
